headline: Hira Walraven Sells the Least Visible Part of a Saudi MEP Package
deck: A Dubai manufacturer and a Dutch fixings group have spent years building a regional pipe support business. The product is a bracket, and the argument is that brackets are where MEP installations quietly fail.
excerpt: Hira Walraven, formed from Hira Industries' fixing systems division and the Netherlands-based Walraven Group, supplies pipe supports, seismic bracing and anchors across Gulf MEP projects. Its Saudi references include the HVAC, plumbing and firefighting installations at Princess Nourah bint Abdulrahman University in Riyadh.
content:
Every mechanical, electrical and plumbing package in a Saudi building contains thousands of components nobody looks at. Pipe supports, hangers, channel, brackets, clamps, anchors and seismic bracing hold the chilled water pipework, the drainage, the fire main and the cable containment in position for the life of the building. They are a small fraction of the package value and a disproportionate share of its failure modes.

Hira Walraven exists to sell that category properly. It was formed from the fixing systems division of Hira Industries, the Dubai-based manufacturer established in 1980 that now employs more than 1,000 people with offices across the Middle East, together with the Walraven Group of the Netherlands, and it opened a dedicated facility in the United Arab Emirates reported at $5.4 million. The product range covers pipe support systems, channel and strut, anchors and seismic bracing, sold into plumbing, HVAC and fire protection.

The Saudi track record is a genuine reference rather than a brochure claim. Diamond pipe supports were used on the HVAC, plumbing and firefighting installations at Princess Nourah bint Abdulrahman University in Riyadh, one of the largest single university campuses built in the Kingdom. That is the kind of reference a Saudi consultant actually checks: a completed project, at scale, in the same climate, still operating.

The wider Hira group sits across several adjacent categories that turn up in the same riser — Aerofoam thermal insulation, Aeroduct ducting accessories, Maico ventilation products and RubTech rubber products among them — which gives it the position of a supplier that can serve most of a mechanical package from one relationship. In a market where a contractor's biggest procurement risk is coordinating deliveries from a dozen suppliers against one installation sequence, that consolidation has a value of its own.

The technical case for taking supports seriously is stronger than their cost share suggests. A pipe support carries dead load, thermal movement, vibration from pumps and, in a chilled water system, a thermal break — because a metal bracket clamped directly onto a cold pipe conducts heat straight through the insulation and produces condensation at the one point in the system where nobody is looking. Corrosion at the support is a common origin of leaks in Gulf plant rooms. Undersized or badly spaced supports produce sagging, joint stress and noise transmission. And the seismic bracing question, historically ignored in parts of the region, is now a code compliance matter that consultants check.

That is the Saudi angle that matters. The Saudi Building Code has become a real constraint on how mechanical services are installed rather than a paper reference, and it is prominent enough in the market that navigating it is a topic area in the conference programme at Big 5 Construct Saudi this week. A supports supplier that can demonstrate tested load ratings, corrosion protection classes and compliant bracing designs is selling compliance evidence, not steel.

The commercial context is a Saudi MEP market expanding rapidly on the back of the giga-project pipeline, the housing programme and industrial development, with industrial MEP services alone forecast around $8.5 billion over the second half of the decade. Volume of that kind is what makes regional manufacturing of a commodity-adjacent product viable: supports are heavy, bulky, cheap per unit and expensive to ship, which is close to a textbook case for producing near the market rather than importing.

For buyers walking the halls at Riyadh Front, the questions on a supports stand are the same as everywhere else on the floor — test certificates, corrosion class, stock held inside the Kingdom, delivery against a fixed programme, and whether an engineer will come out and look at a bracing layout. They are unglamorous questions about an unglamorous product, and they decide whether a mechanical installation is still watertight in fifteen years.
author: BrentDesk Staff
seoTitle: Hira Walraven Sells the Bracket Nobody Looks At
seoDescription: Pipe supports and seismic bracing are a small share of an MEP package and a large share of its failures. Hira Walraven's Saudi references go back years.
